rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That Book’ may be the Scripture promised through Moses and Jesus, or the book signaled by the opening letters alif lām mīm.
rows.anchor: ذلك الكتاب الذى وعد به على لسان موسى وعيسى عليهما السلام أو ذلك إشارة إلى الم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine demonstrative can refer to the feminine sūra because its predicate is ‘the Book’; as an adjective it points directly to the masculine noun book.
rows.anchor: وإن كان صفته فالاشارة به إلى الكتاب صريحا لأن اسم الاشارة مشار به إلى الجنس الواقع صفة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If alif lām mīm names the sūra, it may be a subject followed by a second subject and predicate, or a report with an omitted subject; if it is a sound, ‘that Book’ is subject and predicate.
rows.anchor: أن يكون الم مبتدأ وذلك مبتدأ ثانيا والكتاب خبره والجملة خبر للمبتدأ الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it the Book means it is complete, with other books comparatively deficient, like calling someone ‘the man’ for full manliness.
rows.anchor: ومعناه أن ذلك هو الكتاب الكامل كأن ما عداه من الكتب فى مقابلته ناقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rayb is doubt that makes a person inwardly uneasy and unsettled; the verb rābanī means it caused such unease.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة الريبة قلق النفس واضطرابها ومنه قوله عليه السلام دع ما يريبك إلى مالا يريبك

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet counsels leaving what causes doubt for what does not; doubt unsettles the soul, while truth and soundness bring reassurance. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه السلام دع ما يريبك إلى مالا يريبك فان الشك ريبة وان الصدق طمأنينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exhaustive negation means the Qur’an gives no proper ground for doubt because its proof is clear, not that nobody has ever doubted it.
rows.anchor: من وضوح الدلالة له وسطوع البرهان بحيث لا ينبغى لمرتاب أن يقع فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting ‘doubt’ before ‘in it’ denies doubt of this book and affirms its truth; reversing the order could imply another book has no doubt. He contrasts this with 37:47.
rows.anchor: ولو أولى الظرف لقصد إلى ما يعد عن المراد وهو أن كتابا آخر فيه ريب لافيه

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: The common pause is after ‘in it’; Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim pause after ‘doubt,’ requiring the predicate ‘in it’ to be supplied.
rows.anchor: والوقف على فيه هو المشهور وعن نافع وعاصم أنهما وقفا على ريب ولا بد للواقف من أن ينوى خبرا

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: The Meccan reader lengthens the hāʾ in fīhi throughout; Ḥafṣ agrees in fīhi mahānan. Sibawayh objects that this combines three still letters, treating the weak hāʾ like a still letter.
rows.anchor: فيه باشباع كل هاء مكى ووافقه حفص فى فيه مهانا وهو الأصل كقولك مررت به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudā is a verbal noun meaning guidance that leads to the goal; its contrast with misguidance is illustrated by 2:16.
rows.anchor: والهدى مصدر على فعل كالبكا وهو الدلالة الموصلة إلى البغية بدليل وقوع الضلالة فى مقابلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is guidance for the God-fearing though they are already guided, as a request for continued or increased guidance, like ‘Guide us to the straight path’ (1:6).
rows.anchor: تريد طلب الزيادة على ما هو ثابت فيه واستدامته كقوله اهدنا الصراط المستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are called God-fearing as they approach taking up the garment of piety, just as one may name someone for a state he is nearing.
rows.anchor: ولأنه سماهم عند مشارفتهم لا كتساء لباس التقوى متقين كقوله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet’s statement that whoever kills an enemy receives the slain man’s gear illustrates naming someone by a state he approaches; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: من قتل قتيلا فله سلبه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās advises anyone intending pilgrimage to hasten, since illness may befall; this likewise names someone by an impending state. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وقول ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما إذا أراد احدكم الحج فليعجل فإنه يمرض المريض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is not called guidance for the astray because some are known to persist in error while others are known to reach guidance; the book guides the latter, compressed in this wording.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل هدى للضالين لأنهم فريقان فريق علم بقاءهم على الضلالة وفريق علم أن مصيرهم إلى الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwā derives from waqā, ‘to protect’: the root’s wāw changes to tāʾ and assimilates in iftaʿala, yielding ittaqā; the noun denotes intense protection.
rows.anchor: والمتقى فى اللغة اسم فاعل من قولهم وقاه فاتقى ففاؤها واو ولامها ياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In religious usage, the God-fearing person guards against doing or omitting what merits punishment.
rows.anchor: وفى الشريعة من يقى نفسه تعاطى ما يستحق به العقوبة من فعل أو ترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudā may be nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject or of lā rayba fīhi, or accusative as a circumstantial qualifier of the pronoun in fīhi.
rows.anchor: ومحل هدى الرفع لأنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف أو خبر مع لا ريب فيه لذلك أو النصب على الحال

words: ذَٰلِكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبُ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ هُدًۭى لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads four unjoined clauses as tightly linked: the challenge, the complete Book, its certainty, then its guidance; each develops the preceding one.
rows.anchor: وقد أصيب بترتيبها مفصل البلاغة حيث جئ بها متناسقة هكذا من غير حرف عطف

words: ذَٰلِكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبُ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ هُدًۭى لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence uses ellipsis, the grandeur of the definite article, and the placing of doubt before ‘in it’; hudā is an indefinite verbal noun, as if the Book itself were guidance beyond full comprehension.
rows.anchor: وفى الرابعة الحذف ووضع المصدر الذى هو هدى موضع الوصف الذى هو هاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing believers, unbelievers, and hypocrites and their outcomes, God turns to direct address, an instance of iltifāt.
rows.anchor: لما عدد الله فرق المكلفين من المؤمنين والكفار والمنافقين وذكر صفاتهم وأحوالهم

rows.speaker: علقمة
rows.claim: ʿAlqama says Qur’anic ‘O people’ addresses Meccans, while ‘O you who believe’ addresses Medinans; al-Nasafī identifies this call as directed to Meccan polytheists.
rows.anchor: قال علقمة ما فى القرآن يا أيها الناس فهو خطاب لأهل مكة وما فيه يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو خطاب لأهل المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ‘O people’ addresses the polytheists of Mecca.
rows.anchor: وهذا خطاب لمشركى مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yāʾ is conventionally for a distant addressee and ayyuha with hamza for a near one; it is also used for the heedless as if distant, making a call to someone nearby emphatic.
rows.anchor: فذاك للتوكيد المؤذن بأن الخطاب الذى يتلوه معتنى به جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the nearby ‘O Lord’ expresses the caller’s self-abasement and distance from divine nearness despite longing for a response.
rows.anchor: واستبعاد لها عن مظان الزلفى هظما لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayyu connects a vocative to a definite noun or description, as dhū and alladhī connect generic nouns or clauses; ayyu is ambiguous and needs a following clarifying descriptor.
rows.anchor: فلا بد أن يردفه اسم جنس أو ما يجرى مجراه يتصف به حتى يتضح المقصود بالنداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike Zayd, ayyu cannot stand independently; the following noun or clause describes it, and interposed hāʾ of alerting emphasizes the call and compensates for absent annexation.
rows.anchor: إلا أن أيا لا يستقل بنفسه استقلال زيد فمم ينفك عن الصفة وكلمة التنبيه المقحمة بين الصفة وموصوفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an repeatedly uses this emphatic form because its commands, prohibitions, promises, and threats are weighty while people are heedless.
rows.anchor: وكثر النداء فى القرآن على هذه الطريقة لأن ما نادى الله به عباده من اوامره ونواهيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Worship your Lord’ means affirm His oneness.
rows.anchor: وحدوه قال ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما كل عبادة فى القرآن فهى توحيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says every act of worship mentioned in the Qur’an is tawḥīd.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما كل عبادة فى القرآن فهى توحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Creator is the one who brings the nonexistent into being according to measure and proportion.
rows.anchor: والخلق إيجاد المعدوم على تقدير واستواء

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila define creation as bringing a thing into being according to measure and proportion, since they regard the nonexistent as a thing that can be known and described.
rows.anchor: وعند المعتزلة إيجاد الشىء على تقدير واستواء وهذا بناء على أن المعدوم شيء عندهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nasafī’s position is that ‘thing’ names what exists.
rows.anchor: وعندنا هو اسم للموجود

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads khalaqakum with assimilation.
rows.anchor: خلقكم بالادغام أبو عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the audience already acknowledged God as creator of them and their predecessors, they are urged to worship Him rather than idols.
rows.anchor: احتج عليهم بانه خالقهم وخالق من قبلهم لأنهم كانوا مقرين بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is enjoined in hope that they will thereby become God-fearing and escape punishment; from a generous giver, inducement by laʿalla functions like a firm promise.
rows.anchor: أى اعبدوا على رجاء أن تتقوا فتنجوا بسببه من العذاب ولعل للترجى والاطماع

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh treats laʿalla here as hope or inducement, which from a generous speaker functions like a binding promise.
rows.anchor: ولكنه إطماع من كريم فيجرى مجرى وعده المحتوم وفاؤه وبه قال سيبويه

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Quṭrub reads laʿalla as ‘so that,’ expressing purpose.
rows.anchor: وقال قطرب هو بمعنى كى أى لكى تتقوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jaʿala means ‘made’ or ‘rendered.’
rows.anchor: أى صير ومحل الذى نصب على المدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhī may be accusative as a praise construction or nominative as the subject of an understood huwa.
rows.anchor: ومحل الذى نصب على المدح أو رفع باضمار هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Firāsh means a spread-out resting place for sitting, sleeping, and moving; it is the second object of jaʿala.
rows.anchor: بساطا تقعدون عليها وتنامون وتتقلبون وهو مفعول ثان لجعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling earth a spread does not prove it flat rather than spherical, since spreading and resting on it are possible on either account.
rows.anchor: وليس فيه دليل على أن الأرض مسطحة أو كرية إذ الافتراش ممكن على التقديرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is a roof; bināʾ is a verbal noun used for the built structure. He links this to 21:32.
rows.anchor: سقفا كقوله تعالى وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا وهو مصدر سمى به المبنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water sent down from the sky is rain.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأنزل من السماء ماء ﴾ مطرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fruits emerge through God’s power, will, and creation; He makes water a cause, like reproductive fluid in a child’s creation, though He can create without causes, which He created along with matter.
rows.anchor: ولكن جعل الماء سببا فى خروجها كماء الفحل فى خلق الولد وهو قادر على إنشاء الكل بلا سبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating things gradually through successive states and stages contains wisdom and lessons for observers with insight.
rows.anchor: ولكن له فى إنشاء الأشياء مدرجا لها من حال إلى حال وناقلا من مرتبة إلى مرتبة حكما وعبرا للنظار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is partitive or explanatory; rizqan is a purpose object with the partitive reading and a direct object of akhraja with the explanatory reading.
rows.anchor: للتبعيض أو للبيان ﴿ رزقا ﴾ مفعول له إن كانت للتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamarāt is used instead of thamar or thimār because the intended sense is a collection of fruits and plural forms interchange where both indicate collectivity.
rows.anchor: لأن المراد جماعة الثمرة و لأن الجموع يتعاور بعضها موقع بعض لالتقائها فى الجمعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lakum modifies rizq if rizq means the provision itself; if it means the act of providing, it is an object, ‘providing you.’
rows.anchor: صفة جارية على الرزق إن أريد به العين وإن جعل اسما للمعنى فهو مفعول به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition follows the command to worship: tawḥīd is the basis of worship, so no equal or partner may be assigned to God.
rows.anchor: هو متعلق بالأمر أى اعبدوا ربكم فلا تجعلوا له أندادا لأن أصل العبادة وأساسها التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, alladhī is a subject whose predicate is the prohibition; the fāʾ introduces the consequence implicit in the discourse: since God surrounded them with signs, they should not take partners.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الذى رفعا على الابتداء وخبره فلا تجعلوا ودخول الفاء لأن الكلام يتضمن الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nidd is an equal, specifically an opposing rival; denying God a nidd or ḍidd denies both an equivalent substitute and an antagonist.
rows.anchor: والند المثل ولا يقال إلا للمثل المخالف والمناوئ ومعنى قولهم ليس لله ند ولا ضد نفى ما يسد مسده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The audience knows idols neither create nor provide while God is creator and provider; alternatively, the object of ‘know’ is omitted, meaning they are people of knowledge and idolatry is utter ignorance.
rows.anchor: انها لا تخلق شيئا ولا ترزق والله الخالق الرازق أو مفعول تعلمون متروك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels declare God beyond anything being hidden from Him and beyond objection to His governance.
rows.anchor: تنزيها لك أن يخفى عليك شيء أو عن الاعتراض عليك فى تدبيرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that knowledge of the names surpasses what is attainable through worship; knowledge of the divine law is all the more so.
rows.anchor: فكيف بعلم الشريعة انتصابه على المصدر تقديره سبحت الله تسبيحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subḥāna is accusative as a cognate verbal noun, with the implied phrase ‘I glorify God with glorification.’
rows.anchor: انتصابه على المصدر تقديره سبحت الله تسبيحا

words: لَا عِلْمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَآ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā means ‘that which’ and ʿilm means ‘known object’: we know nothing except what You taught us.
rows.anchor: أى لا معلوم لنا إلى الذى علمتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAlīm is the one who is not taught; al-Ḥakīm is wise in what He decrees and determines.
rows.anchor: غير المعلم ﴿ الحكيم ﴾ فيما قضيت وقدرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf may be ism inna and anta the subject of a clause with two predicates; alternatively, anta is a separator and the two names are predicates.
rows.anchor: أنت فصل والخبر العلم والحكيم خبر ثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza calls the audience to account while expressing rebuke and astonishment at their conduct.
rows.anchor: للتقرير مع التوبيخ والتعجب من حالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birr is breadth of good and recognized virtue, from spaciousness, and includes every good; the idiom ‘you were truthful and dutiful’ exemplifies it.
rows.anchor: أى سعة الخير والمعورف ومنه البر لسعته ويتناول كل خير

rows.speaker: الأحبار
rows.claim: The rabbis privately told relatives and others to follow Muḥammad, but did not follow him themselves.
rows.anchor: من أقاربهم وغيرهم باتباع محمد عليه السلام ولا يتبعونه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says they urged charity but did not give it themselves and misappropriated charity collected for distribution.
rows.anchor: كانوا يأمرون بالصدقة ولا يتصدقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting themselves means leaving their own share of goodness as if they were forgotten.
rows.anchor: وتتركونها من البر كالمنسيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a rebuke: they read the Torah, which describes Muḥammad, or warns against betrayal, abandoning goodness, and letting conduct contradict speech.
rows.anchor: وفيها نعت محمد عليه السلام أو فيها الوعيد على الخيانة وترك البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes them severely for failing to recognize their ugly conduct and let that recognition restrain them.
rows.anchor: أفلا تفطنون لقبيح ما أقدمتم عليه حتى يصدكم استقباحه عن ارتكابه وهو توبيخ عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Man is a subject in an interrogative and aẓlam its predicate: who is more unjust, meaning none is more unjust.
rows.anchor: موضع من رفع على الابتداء وهو استفهام وأظلم خبره والمعنى أى أحد أظلم

words: مَنَعَ مَسَٰجِدَ ٱللَّهِ أَن يُذْكَرَ فِيهَا ٱسْمُهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An yudhkara is the second object of manaʿa; the preposition may be omitted before an, or an may express purpose, ‘for fear that His name be mentioned.’
rows.anchor: وأن يذكر ثانى مفعولى منع لأنك تقول منعته كذا ومثله وما منعنا أن نرسل بالآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruling applies generally to God’s mosques: anyone who prevents remembrance in them is exceedingly unjust, although the reported occasion concerns one mosque.
rows.anchor: هو حكم عام لجنس مساجد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported occasion is that Christians damaged Jerusalem’s sanctuary and prevented people from praying there.
rows.anchor: والسبب فيه طرح النصارى فى بيت المقدس الأذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported occasion is the polytheists’ preventing the Messenger from entering the Sacred Mosque at al-Ḥudaybiyya.
rows.anchor: أو منع المشركين رسول الله أن يدخل المسجد الحرام عام الحديبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is general although the occasion is specific, as in 104:1, ‘Woe to every slanderer,’ revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Sharīq.
rows.anchor: والمنزول فيه الأخنس بن شريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking to ruin the mosques means causing remembrance there to cease; the intended sense is general like ‘God’s mosques.’
rows.anchor: بانقطاع الذكر والمراد عن العموم كما اريد العموم بمساجد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who bar worship should enter only in fear and trembling that believers might overpower them, rather than seizing mosques and barring believers.
rows.anchor: أى ما كان ينبغى لهم أن يدخلوا مساجد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse prohibits Muslims from enabling them to enter or leaving them free to do so, paralleling the construction in 33:53.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه النهى عن تمكينهم من الدخول والتخلية بينهم وبينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Christians entered Jerusalem’s sanctuary only in disguise, fearing they would be killed; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: روى أنه لا يدخل بيت المقدس أحد من النصارى إلا متنكرا خيفة أن يقتل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says any Christian found in Jerusalem was beaten severely; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة لا يوجد نصرانى فى بيت المقدس إلا بولغ ضربا

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Messenger announced that after that year no polytheist would make pilgrimage; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: ونادى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ألا لا يحجن بعد هذا العام مشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly disgrace means killing and captivity for a belligerent non-Muslim, and the humiliation of paying jizya for a protected non-Muslim.
rows.anchor: قتل وسبى للحربى وذلة بضرب الجزية للذمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great punishment in the hereafter is the Fire.
rows.anchor: أى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet repeatedly turned his face and shifted his gaze toward the sky.
rows.anchor: تردد وجهك وتصرف نظرك فى جهة السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet expected to be turned toward the Kaʿba, to follow Abraham, distinguish himself from the Jews, and attract Arabs to faith because the sanctuary was their pride and pilgrimage center.
rows.anchor: يتوقع من ربه أن يحوله إلى الكعبة موافقة لإبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nu walliyannaka may mean ‘give and enable you to face it,’ or ‘make you turn toward its direction rather than Jerusalem.’
rows.anchor: فلنعطينك ولنمكننك من استقبالها من قولك وليته كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The desired qibla is one the Prophet loves and inclines toward for sound purposes that accord with God’s will and wisdom.
rows.anchor: تحبها وتميل اليها لأغراضك الصحيحة التى أضمرتها ووافقت مشيئة الله وحكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shatr means toward; it is an adverbial accusative, directing the face toward the mosque’s direction, since exact alignment is difficult for someone far away.
rows.anchor: أى نحوه وشطر نصب على الظرف أى اجعل تولية الوجه تلقاء المسجد أى فى جهته وسمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the Sacred Mosque rather than the Kaʿba indicates that distant worshippers must face its general direction, not its exact physical point.
rows.anchor: وذكر المسجد الحرام دون الكعبة دليل على أن الواجب مراعاة الجهة دون العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for ten months after arriving in Medina, then was turned toward the Kaʿba; no authority or grading is given.
rows.anchor: روى أنه عليه السلام قدم المدينة فصلى نحو بيت المقدس سنة عشر شهرا ثم وجه إلى الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wherever on earth people are, when they intend to pray they must face the Sacred Mosque’s direction.
rows.anchor: من الأرض وأردتم الصلاة ﴿ فولوا وجوهكم شطره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of the Book know the turn toward the Kaʿba is true because their prophets’ glad tidings said the Messenger would pray toward both qiblas.
rows.anchor: أى التحويل إلى الكعبة هو الحق لأنه كان فى بشارة انبيائهم برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه يصلى إلى القبلتين

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: The phrase is read with yāʾ by the Meccan reader, Abū ʿAmr, Nāfiʿ, and ʿĀṣim; others read it with tāʾ.
rows.anchor: ونافع وعاصم وبالتاء غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ reading threatens unbelievers with punishment for rejection, while the tāʾ reading promises believers reward for acceptance and performance.
rows.anchor: وعد للمؤمنين بالثواب على القبول والأداء

rows.speaker: أعرابي
rows.claim: An Arab asked whether their Lord was near so they could speak privately or far so they should call aloud; the verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: ولما قال اعرابى لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أقريب ربنا فنناجيه أم بعيد فنناديه نزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is near in knowledge and answering prayer, not spatial location, since He is exalted above being located.
rows.anchor: علما واجابة لتعاليه عن القرب مكانا

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl and Yaʿqūb retain the yāʾ of daʿānī both in pause and continuation; Abū ʿAmr and Nāfiʿ other than Qālūn do so in continuation, while the rest omit it in both.
rows.anchor: الداعي دعانى فى الحالين سهل ويعقوب ووافقهما أبو عمرو ونافع غير قالون فى الوصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s promise to answer prayer is true and unfailing, but answering a prayer differs from granting the requested need.
rows.anchor: ثم إجابة الدعاء وعد صدق من الله لا خلف فيه غير أن إجابة الدعوة تخالف قضاء الحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Answering is God’s ‘At your service, My servant’ when a believer calls; granting the request may be immediate, delayed, in the hereafter, or replaced by what is better.
rows.anchor: فاجابة الدعوة أن يقول العبد يا رب فيقول الله لبيك عبدى وهذا أمر موعود موجود لكل مؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should respond when God calls them to faith and obedience, just as He answers when they call Him with their needs.
rows.anchor: إذا دعوتهم للايمان والطاعة كما انى أجيبهم إذا دعونى لحوائجهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in ‘let them believe in Me’ is an imperative particle.
rows.anchor: واللام فيها للأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laʿalla expresses hope that they attain right guidance, the opposite of error.
rows.anchor: ليكونوا على رجاء من إصابة الرشد وهو ضد الغى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they stop associating partners with God and fighting, God forgives their past transgression and mercifully accepts their repentance and faith.
rows.anchor: عن الشرك والقتال ﴿ فإن الله غفور ﴾ لما سلف من طغيانهم ﴿ رحيم ﴾ بقبول توبتهم وإيمانهم

rows.speaker: الأخنس بن شريق
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Sharīq: he spoke sweetly to the Messenger, professed love and Islam, and claimed God knew he was sincere.
rows.anchor: كان الأخنس بن شريق حلو المنطق إذا لقى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ألان له القول وادعى أنه يحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His speech pleases and impresses; the root sense is something marvelous that looms large in the mind.
rows.anchor: يروقك ويعظم فى قلبك ومنه الشئ العجيب الذى يعظم فى النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may modify ‘his speech’: he seeks worldly advantage through professed love, not the afterlife; or it may modify ‘pleases you’: his eloquence charms in this life but fails him in the next.
rows.anchor: فى يتعلق بالقول أى يعجبك ما يقوله فى معنى الدنيا لأنه يطلب بادعاء المحبة حظ الدنيا

words: وَيُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِى قَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He swears, saying that God witnesses the love and Islam in his heart.
rows.anchor: أى يحلف ويقول الله شاهد على ما في قلبي من محبتك ومن الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aladd means intensely contentious and hostile to Muslims; al-khiṣām may be a verbal noun (‘in disputation’) or a plural of khaṣm, ‘opponent.’
rows.anchor: شديد الجدال والعداوة للمسلمين والخصام المخاصمة والإضافة بمعنى فى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If khiṣām is a verbal noun, the construction means ‘most contentious in disputation’; if it is the plural of khaṣm, it means ‘the fiercest of opponents in contention.’
rows.anchor: فتقديره ألد فى الخصومة أو الخصام جمع خصم كصعب وصعاب والتقدير وهو أشد الخصوم خصومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawallā means turning away from the Prophet and going off after softening his speech.
rows.anchor: عنك وذهب بعد إلانه القول واحلاء المطنق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Akhnas acted against Thaqīf after a dispute with them: he raided at night, killed their livestock, and burned their crops.
rows.anchor: كما فعل بثقيف فإنه كان بينه وبينهم خصومة فبيتهم ليلا وأهلك مواشيهم وأحرق زروعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥarth and al-nasl mean crops and livestock; the verse may describe destructive conduct by a ruler as well as al-Akhnas’s raid.
rows.anchor: أى الزرع والحيوان أو إذا كان واليا فعل ما يفعله ولاة السوء من الفساد فى الأرض

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says he displays injustice until God withholds rain as a consequence, destroying crops and livestock.
rows.anchor: وقيل يظهر الظلم حتى يمنع الله بشؤم ظلمه القطر فيهلك الحرث والنسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not love corruption.
rows.anchor: والله لا يحب الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person addressed is al-Akhnas, told to fear God regarding his corruption and destruction.
rows.anchor: للأخنس ﴿ اتق الله ﴾ فى الإفساد والإهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression may mean pride and pre-Islamic zeal compel him to commit the sin he is warned against, or that pride seizes him because of the unbelief in his heart.
rows.anchor: وحميّة الجاهلية على الإثم الذى ينهى عنه وألزمته ارتكابه أو الباء للسبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is enough for him and is the wretched resting place, like a bed.
rows.anchor: أى كافيه ﴿ ولبئس المهاد ﴾ أى الفراش جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another occasion is Suhayb’s escape: polytheists tried to make him abandon Islam, killed companions with him, and accepted his wealth in exchange for his release and journey to Medina.
rows.anchor: ونزل فى صهيب حين أراده المشركون على ترك الإسلام وقتلوا نفرا كانوا معه فاشترى نفسه بما له منهم وأتى المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may also concern someone who enjoins right and forbids wrong until he is killed.
rows.anchor: أو فيمن يأمر بالمعروف وينهى عن المنكر حتى يقتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divorced women intended are those with whom the marriage was consummated and who menstruate.
rows.anchor: أراد المدخول بهن من ذوات الإقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declarative form means a command; it strengthens the order by presenting compliance as already occurring, like a prayer phrased as a confident report of fulfillment.
rows.anchor: خبر فى معنى الأمر وأصل الكلام ولتتربص المطلقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal sentence adds emphasis by suggesting permanence, while mention of their own selves stirs women to master desire and wait.
rows.anchor: وفى ذكر الأنفس تهييج لهن على التربص وزيادة بعث لأن أنفس النساء طوامح إلى الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurūʾ means menstruations, supported by reports directing women to leave prayer during their periods and setting a slave woman’s waiting period at two menstruations.
rows.anchor: جمع قرء أو قرء وهو الحيض لقوله عليه السلام دعى الصلاة أيام اقرائك

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says to leave prayer during the days of one’s periods; al-Nasafī cites this as evidence that qurūʾ means menstruation. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: لقوله عليه السلام دعى الصلاة أيام اقرائك

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says a slave woman’s divorce is two and her waiting period is two menstruations; this supports the menstrual sense. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وقوله طلاق الأمة تطليقتان وعدتها حيضتان ولم يقل طهران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waiting months for women who no longer menstruate in 65:4 replace menstruations, not intervals of purity, supporting his reading of qurūʾ as menses.
rows.anchor: فأقام الأشهر مقام الحيض دون الإطهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of waiting is to establish that the womb is empty, which menstruation reveals; an enslaved woman’s waiting is likewise measured by a menstruation.
rows.anchor: العدة استبراء الرحم والحيض هو الذى يستبرأ به الأرحام دون الطهر

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī reads qurūʾ as intervals of purity; al-Nasafī argues that this can end the waiting period at two periods and part of the third, so the prescribed three are not completed.
rows.anchor: كما قال الشافعى لا نقضت العدة بقرأين وبعض الثالث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On al-Nasafī’s view, divorce at the end of menstruation does not count toward the waiting period, whereas al-Shāfiʿī counts divorce at the end of purity; three is a fixed number, not fewer.
rows.anchor: فذا غير محسوب من العدة عندنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thalāthata is either a direct object, ‘wait for three qurūʾ to pass,’ or an adverbial of duration, ‘wait for a period of three qurūʾ.’
rows.anchor: وانتصاب ثلاثة على أنه مفعول به أى يتربصن مضى ثلاثة قروء أو على الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural of abundance qurūʾ replaces the plural of paucity aqruʾ because the forms overlap in collectivity and qurūʾ was more commonly used.
rows.anchor: ولعل القروء كانت اكثر استعمالا فى جمع قرء من الإقراء فأوثر عليه تنزيلا لقليل الاستعمال منزلة المهمل

words: وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَهُنَّ أَن يَكْتُمْنَ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ فِىٓ أَرْحَامِهِنَّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What they might conceal is a child, menstrual blood, or both: a woman seeking separation could hide pregnancy to avoid delayed divorce or her husband relenting, or hide menstruation and falsely claim purity to hasten divorce.
rows.anchor: من الولد أو من دم الحيض أو منهما وذلك إذا أرادت المرأة فراق زوجها فكتمت حملها

words: إِن كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Invoking belief in God and the Last Day magnifies the warning: one who believes in God and His punishment would not dare such grave acts.
rows.anchor: لأن من امن بالله وبعقابه لا يجترئ على مثله من العظائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buʿūla is the plural of baʿl, with the feminine tāʾ marking the plural.
rows.anchor: البعول جمع بعل والتاء لاحقة لتأنيث الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their husbands are more entitled to take them back; calling them husbands after divorce shows that a revocable divorce does not itself prohibit intercourse.
rows.anchor: أى أزواجهن أولى برجعتهن وفيه دليل على أن الطلاق الرجعى لا يحرم الوطء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Within that’ means during the waiting period.
rows.anchor: فى مدة ذلك التربص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the husband seeks reconciliation and the wife refuses, his decision prevails; she has no independent right to refuse the return.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أن الرجل إن أراد الرجعة وأبتها المرأة وجب إيثار قوله على قولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The husband’s superior right applies when he seeks reconciliation and kindness, not harm to his wife.
rows.anchor: لما بينهم وبينهن وإحسانا إليهن ولم يريدوا مضارتهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Women have duties corresponding in goodness to their rights, in a manner recognized by religious law and custom; neither spouse may impose what is not owed.
rows.anchor: بالوجه الذى لا ينكر فى الشرع وعادات الناس فلا يكلف أحد الزوجين صاحبه ما ليس له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Equality concerns the comparable goodness of obligations, not identical tasks: if she washes or bakes for him, he need not do the same, but reciprocates suitably as a man.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالمماثلة مماثلة الواجب فى كونه حسنه لا فى جنس الفعل فلا يجب عليه إذا غسلت ثيابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The men’s degree may be their additional right and merit in managing her affairs, or their maintenance and control of the marriage bond.
rows.anchor: فى اللذة والاستمتاع أو بالانفاق وملك النكاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty, beyond challenge in His affairs, and wise, commanding only what is right and good.
rows.anchor: لا يامر إلا بما هو صواب وحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If fear comes from an enemy or another cause, the worshipper prays while walking.
rows.anchor: فإن كان بكم خوف من عدو أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijālan is a circumstantial accusative meaning on foot; it is the plural of rājil, like qāʾim/qiyām.
rows.anchor: حال أى فصلوا راجلين وهو جمع راجل كقائم وقيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fearful may pray mounted, with gestures; facing the qibla is waived.
rows.anchor: وحدانا بإيماء ويسقط عنه التوجه إلى القبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Security means the fear has ended.
rows.anchor: فإذا زال خوفكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When safe, remember God by performing the normal prayer of security.
rows.anchor: فصلوا صلاة الأمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember God in the way He taught you, including the ordinary prayer you had not known before His instruction.
rows.anchor: أى ذكرا مثل ما علمكم
